# OUT-1 — Decisions rows D407 to D425

**Append these rows to the bottom of `docs/decisions.md`, in order, after D406. Do not edit any old row, its text or its status cell.** Format: ID | date | decision | source | status. All rows are dated 2026-10-21. D407 is the owner's sweep (Decided). D408 to D424 are **Proposed**. **D425 is added only after the owner has said yes in the Claude Code thread** (see the note at the end). Row numbers are the ones the other files quote.

| ID | Date | Decision | Source | Status |

| D407 | 2026-10-21 | **The Proposed sweep, recorded in one row, like D385 (owner, 2026-10-21; old rows are not edited).** The owner accepted every group below *as described*. **Group A (v0.9 design rows):** D358–D366, D368, D370, D371, D373–D379, D382 and D384; and, **in their amended form,** D367 (as amended by D396's alternation and D404's rows), D369, D372 (replaced by D400, which is Decided), D380 and D381 (both changed by D398) and D383. **Group B:** D388–D396. **Group C:** D387, D397, D398, D399, D402 and D403. **Amended rows are accepted as amended:** a reader follows the later row that changes them. D400, D401, D404, D405 and D406 are already Decided and need nothing. **No old row's text or status cell is edited.** **Check after applying:** every `\| Proposed \|` row with an id from D358 to D406 must be named above; every one with an id from D408 up is a new v0.10 row; rows below D358 are D385's and are not checked. | D408 | 2026-10-21 | **What Orders are for (v0.10 flesh-out; the owner's answer to Q1).** Orders are **story first, with a choice that has a cost,** not a power tree. The cost is a **limited number of seats** (D412), so the player chooses whose story advances and whose small perk applies. Each Order gives a short questline (D414) and one small number plus one story or knowledge perk per level (D411). **No Order gives silver income, a fight number or a gate** (D418). The Orders are the four of lore §14: the Thanes' Moot, the Grey Wives, the Bell-Watchers and the Quenchers. The open questions in GDD §5.13 (exclusivity; whether reputation persists through the Long Night) are answered by D409 and D410. | v0.10 flesh-out, Q1 | Proposed |
| D409 | 2026-10-21 | **Orders are not exclusive in what you earn; they are limited in what is active (owner's answer to Q2).** (1) **All four Orders are always open to earn standing in** once each has opened (D413); standing is never lost and is not tied to a seat. (2) **Only a seated Order gives its perks and advances its questline.** An unseated Order keeps its standing and its due chapters, and they wait (D414); a waiting chapter never blocks another Order's. (3) **The Moot and the Quenchers are an opposed pair** (lore §14, §5): their **last chapters end differently** by whether the other is also seated (D414), and **each last chapter waits until the other Order has opened,** so no one is locked into an ending before the other side exists. (4) **Nothing required can come only from an Order** (lore §8): no required name, document, bestiary entry or Legendary is Order-only, and every Order's story is completable eventually by seating it. (5) The Grey Wives' hints and the Bell-Watchers' sharper text (D411) change *where to look*, never what exists. | v0.10 flesh-out, Q2 | Proposed |
| D410 | 2026-10-21 | **How standing is earned (owner's answers to Q3, Q6, Q11; refined at the review).** (1) Standing grows from **play already done,** with no new chores: **Moot** 1 per contract won, any village. **Grey Wives** 1 per brew, 3 per experiment, 10 per property revealed. **Bell-Watchers** 5 per document or hunter letter found, 10 per name found. **Quenchers** 2 per Kozly Hollow contract won; each Delve floor **whose result paid Riftglass** adds 1, capped per 7-day window on the event clock (`orders.delveWeeklyCap`). **Events add nothing in v0.10.** (2) **Each Triumphant stand adds a fixed chunk (`orders.triumphantChunk`) to every Order,** open or not. (3) **Four levels per Order** from thresholds in `balance.ts` (sketches). (4) **Standing never drops and is kept forever through the Long Night;** the highest level reached is saved so tuning can never lower a level. (5) **All four Orders count from v10 on, opened or not,** so nothing is reconstructed when an Order opens; **a save migrated from v9 gets one backfill at the migration, capped at level 1** (`orders.backfillCapLevel`), shown as a "brought from before the Orders" line, so a long-running save starts at the bottom and its first chapters come one at a time. What the save cannot recover starts at 0 and the migration names it (D421). (6) One Orders card shows level and count with a breakdown; **no new tab** (D416). (7) Every weight and threshold is a sketch the Orderer measures (D417). (8) Delve standing is a Delve reward with an idle source (Kozly Hollow contracts), so the Delve-optional test (D20, D271) stays true. | v0.10 flesh-out, Q3, Q6, Q11; review M2, M7, S8, S10 | Proposed |
| D411 | 2026-10-21 | **Perks (owner's answers to Q4 and Q10; refined at the review).** Each level gives **one small number and one story or knowledge perk, only while the Order is seated.** **Moot:** contract provisions food −3% a level (−12% at level 4); heads' lines in notices and a "What the heads say about you" entry on the Villages panel. **Grey Wives:** brew and experiment time −4% a level (−16%), **fixed when the brew or experiment is queued;** a hint toward a brew in the Book from "the eldest Grey Wife", **and an elder's note instead once the Book already holds that brew.** **Bell-Watchers:** clue time −4% a level (−16%); a sharper where-to-look sentence for still-missing names, **built by a stated rule from the roll,** and a remark by Halina or Dana once the group is found (OUT-3 E3). **Quenchers:** the hourly Threat rate −3% a level (−12%); a Kozly Hollow voice added to the Accounts event "What the hearth leaves" (OUT-3 E4). **There is no new bonus bucket (§5.0):** each number is its own named factor with its own breakdown line. **The Quenchers' perk is a trade:** a lower Threat makes each wave weaker (−0.61% Health and Might per point) and also lowers the Embers a stand pays (+0.7% per point of Threat); the Order sheet says so, and the stand preview uses the seated factor and recomputes at a seat change. The stand rows are re-judged on the Orderer (D417). Every step is a tunable named constant, bounded by the locked `orders.perkCeiling` = 20% (D418). | v0.10 flesh-out, Q4, Q10; review S3, S5, S9 | Proposed |
| D412 | 2026-10-21 | **Seats (owner's answers to Q5 and Q16; refined at the review).** (1) **Two seats at the start.** A **third opens only when two Orders are at level 4 and the Quenchers have opened** (both conditions, Q16 (a)); it is **checked after every level change, at the Quenchers' opening and on load,** so it opens whichever happens last; once open it is **kept forever through the Long Night.** The card reads, with the third seat closed: "Seats: 2 of 3 (the third opens when two Orders reach their top level and the Quenchers have come)." and, once open: "Seats: 3 of 3." and a second line "In seats: …" (or "In seats: none"). (2) **Each Order takes one seat; there is no partial seating.** (3) **Swaps are free at each new warden's arrival,** by a skippable **"Seat your Orders"** step on the new-warden sheet where the previous seats carry over by default. (4) **Mid-cycle changes** (seat, unseat or swap) start a **24 h cooldown on the monotone event clock** (`eventNow`, D359, D387), shown as "Can change in 9 h 20 m"; a rewound device clock gives no free change. A new warden's arrival clears it. (5) **Seating into a free seat at an Order's opening does not start the cooldown** (D422). **An opening scene's button reads "Seat it" only if a seat is free;** otherwise it reads "Continue". (6) **On load,** after the opening scenes, the same "Seat your Orders" step appears once as a sheet on the Hold screen (and stays reachable from the Orders card until used), free of cooldown. | v0.10 flesh-out, Q5, Q16; review M4, S6 | Proposed |
| D413 | 2026-10-21 | **When each Order opens, and who speaks for it (owner's answers to Q7 and Q8).** (1) **Each opens for good, with a short scene** (OUT-3 Part C): **Moot** at the first Keep; **Grey Wives** at the first Alchemist's Hut; **Bell-Watchers** at Ilse's arrival; **Quenchers** when D5-08 is found. (2) **Faces are existing people only, so no new person name is introduced:** Moot: the five heads (Marta Dubska, Bohdan Kozel, Ilona Sváteková, Gunnar Ravnsson, Sólveig Arnadóttir), Marta usually; Grey Wives: Vesna as the link, Ostap, and **an unnamed "eldest Grey Wife"**; Bell-Watchers: Halina, Dana Lisová and Ilse; Quenchers: Bohdan Kozel as the voice, Věra sympathising but not joining. (3) **The Quenchers never turn violent:** they argue, petition and refuse, and they are partly right about the dross (lore §14). (4) The Moot's opening uses **no Sending, Deep or "onward" knowledge** (it is spoiler-safe at the first Keep of a new game); the other openings use the same rule apart from "onward", which the setting primer itself uses in public. (5) No lore beyond lore §14 and the existing acts is written without asking (D423). | v0.10 flesh-out, Q7, Q8 | Proposed |
| D414 | 2026-10-21 | **The questlines: sixteen chapters, four per Order (owner's answers to Q12 and Q13; all sixteen outlines approved; refined at the review).** (1) Chapter *n* of an Order is **playable** when the Order is open and **seated,** its level is at least *n,* the previous chapter is read, and its condition holds (OUT-3 Part B); otherwise it **waits** and is never lost. What is playable is **worked out from the state each time** (there is no stored chapter queue), in the order Moot, Grey Wives, Bell-Watchers, Quenchers, then chapter number; an unseated Order's waiting chapter never blocks another's. (2) **The Moot's and the Quenchers' last chapters each have two endings,** by whether the opposed Order is also seated when the chapter is read (variant A: seated; variant B: not), **and each waits until the other Order has opened.** (3) Each chapter is a short scene sheet about the length of the Act VI closing scenes; scenes open **one at a time,** each ending with Close and, if another waits, Next. (4) **No chapter carries a required name or document, and chapter 4 of every Order ends on a threshold** that v0.11 can pick up. (5) Chapters are kept on a new **"Orders" Library shelf,** re-readable, never missable. (6) Titles: Moot, *A table at the gate*, *Salt and a ledger*, *The one who leaves*, *What is it for?*; Grey Wives, *The kettle test*, *Tea for a recipe*, *Two hands*, *What can't be mended*; Bell-Watchers, *The second spring*, *A list of springs*, *What he said at the door*, *A bell of our own*; Quenchers, *Three at the gate*, *Věra's chair*, *A cold supper*, *The mouth*. (7) **Nobody in any chapter says, asks for or begins the Sent's names** (D386); the full texts are OUT-3, word for word. | v0.10 flesh-out, Q12, Q13; review M2, M3, S7 | Proposed |
| D415 | 2026-10-21 | **The final act: a new milestone v0.11 "The Remembering" (owner's answer to Q9; settles D24.10).** (1) **v0.11 comes between Orders (v0.10) and v1.0** and holds The Remembering and the ending. v1.0 stays polish and balance (the plan's v1.0 line about endings is superseded by this row). (2) **v0.10 saves the Orders seated when each chapter was read** (D419), so v0.11 can read what the player stood with. (3) No Order scene says, asks for or begins the Sent's names. (4) **The Act VI closing line "The story continues in a later version" stays through v0.10 and goes when v0.11 ships.** (5) v0.11 is added to the plan as an **outline only;** it gets its own flesh-out session first (plan §0.4). | v0.10 flesh-out, Q9 | Proposed |
| D416 | 2026-10-21 | **Orders screens (owner's answer to Q14; refined at the review).** (1) **One Orders card on the Hold screen,** placed **after the Events card when that card is shown, otherwise after the last card shown** (the Bell-Watchers can open in the Hamlet): the seats lines (D412), each open Order's level word and count, "Seated" or "Not seated", and "A chapter waits for a seat." when a chapter waits. (2) **An Order sheet** per Order: the breakdown of its standing (each source with count, weight and share, and the "brought from before the Orders" line), its four levels with their perks, chapters read, and **Seat / Unseat / Swap** with the cooldown line. (3) **Chapters play as scene sheets** and are kept on the Library's new **Orders** shelf (the Rime pattern). (4) **The Hold tab carries one badge,** shown while a chapter can be read now or an Order with a due chapter is not seated; it is worked out from the state, so it clears when neither is true. (5) The perk lines appear where they act (a breakdown line; the heads' lines in notices; the Book hint; the Names view; the Accounts). (6) **Scene order on one load:** act scenes, the events scene, the Orders opening scenes (Moot, Grey Wives, Bell-Watchers, Quenchers), the "Seat your Orders" sheet, then chapters. (7) **Level names:** Neighbour, Friend, Ally, Kin, not village trust's words. (8) Layouts: no sideways scroll at 360, 900 and 1300 px (a Playwright check). | v0.10 flesh-out, Q14; review S6, S14, S17, N5, N11 | Proposed |
| D417 | 2026-10-21 | **The simulator and the six proposed rows (owner's answer to Q15; refined at the review).** (1) A new player, **the Orderer,** on the **Monday seeds only,** in its own shard. **Every other player never seats an Order,** so their baselines stay put. (2) The Orderer plays like Standard, **and runs Delves as the Delver does once they are open** (so the Delve source and its cap are exercised); it **taps "Seat it" at an opening when a seat is free;** at each new warden it seats the Orders ranked by **(1) chapters playable now, (2) chapters unread, (3) list order** (Moot, Grey Wives, Bell-Watchers, Quenchers); it takes the third seat as soon as it opens, never uses the mid-cycle swap, reads every chapter when playable, and plays until every chapter has played, up to the 42-day cap. (3) **Proposed rows, all on the median of the 5 Monday seeds, held for approval in their own commit:** (a) **chapter 1 of each Order plays within 24 h of its Order opening** (replaces "the first Order opens within 24 h", which cannot fail); (b) every Order reaches level 4 by the end of cycle 6; (c) all 16 chapters have played by the end of cycle 8; (d) the silver share stays at least 70% (§6.3 #6); (e) the provisions share stays in 20–40% with the Moot perk counted (§6.3 #8); (f) with the Quenchers perk on, **"Best Last Stand timing (days 4–5)", "First Long Night (days 3–5)", "Act VI lands in its cycle" and the Dross-Tide stand probe** still pass; the Embers per stand with and without the perk are reported, not judged. (4) The Triumphant chunk, the Delve cap, the thresholds and the weights are sketches. **My rough view is that the Quenchers (open about cycle 5, one village of five, 2 a contract) will not reach 260 by cycle 6 on the sketches;** tune that Order's thresholds and weight first, the Triumphant chunk last (it moves every Order). (5) **If no reasonable tunable passes a row, stop and write it to `docs/questions.md`.** (6) **The Orderer's shard stays within 5 minutes; if it does not, stop and ask** (D320). | v0.10 flesh-out, Q15; review S3, S4, S18 | Proposed |
| D418 | 2026-10-21 | **What does not change in v0.10, and how constants are marked.** (1) **`rulesVersion` stays 5.** No golden fight, recorded fight or recorded stand changes its result; if one does, stop and ask (D308, D344 (1)). (2) **No new bonus bucket** (§5.0), no silver income and no fight number from an Order. (3) **No new random stream** (Orders are deterministic). (4) **Locked:** `orders.seatsStart`, `orders.seatsMax`, `orders.thirdSeatTopOrders`, `orders.levels`, `orders.opposed`, `orders.perkCeiling` (a new locked key; plan §0.6 gets its row at T10.2 from OUT-4b). **Tunable:** the weights, thresholds, `orders.delveWindow`, `orders.delveWeeklyCap`, `orders.triumphantChunk`, `orders.backfillCapLevel`, `orders.swapCooldown` and the four perk steps (GDD §7.12). (5) **No runtime dependency is added.** (6) **The old simulator rows and baselines are unchanged;** only the Orderer sees Orders. (7) **Orders do change `advance`:** standing is added by events inside it (a contract resolves, a brew finishes), the Quenchers' Threat factor works over time inside it, and an Order can open during the away catch-up. A **time-away equivalence test** (one long `advance` equals many short ones) is run with the Quenchers seated. | v0.10 flesh-out; review S2 | Proposed |
| D419 | 2026-10-21 | **Seats are recorded when a chapter is read.** For each chapter the save keeps the list of Orders seated at that moment, **in the fixed order Moot, Grey Wives, Bell-Watchers, Quenchers** (so equality tests are stable), and so which variant played. v0.11 reads this and nothing else from Orders; v0.10 uses it only to pick the two endings and for the Library's "read with …" line. | v0.10 flesh-out, Q9; review N7 | Proposed |
| D420 | 2026-10-21 | **Readings Claude made without asking (the owner can say no to any; the full numbered list is in `docs/flesh-out/v0.10-summary.md`).** (1) The eldest Grey Wife stays **unnamed.** (2) The Moot and Bell-Watcher chapters use **only what the villages know in public** and treat Halina's "I know better now" (D4-08) lightly. (3) Ilona **leaves the room** and Bohdan **refuses politely.** (4) A chapter plays when playable (D414) and waits otherwise. (5) The Moot's and the Quenchers' last chapters have **two endings** and wait for each other's Order to open. (6) The Quenchers' Threat perk applies to the **hourly Rank rate only.** (7) A migrated save's backfill is **capped at level 1.** (8) Level names are **Neighbour, Friend, Ally, Kin.** (9) The Delve link counts a floor whose result paid Riftglass, in a 7-day window. (10) The Orderer replaces row (a) and also runs Delves. (11) The Grey Wives' and Bell-Watchers' story perks fall back to an elder's note or a remark when their hints have nothing left to point at. (12) The Moot perk acts on the food paid as contract provisions at launch (GDD §5.4 step 4). (13) No Order ever seats itself. | v0.10 flesh-out; review | Proposed |
| D421 | 2026-10-21 | **The owner's save arrives (a reading for the owner's yes or no, like D402).** (1) On load, a save past each trigger gets the Order **opened, with its scene, one at a time,** after the away catch-up (order of a load: migrate, catch up, open Orders, check the third seat, show scenes). (2) The **one-time backfill** (D410 (5)) counts the sources the save holds, **capped at level 1;** anything it cannot recover starts at 0 and the migration names it in its warnings and the diagnostics. The owner's own save may be in any act and cycle; the tests derive what should open from the fixture itself. (3) The **"Seat your Orders" sheet** opens once with no cooldown. (4) Nothing about hunters, items, Legendary, events or the story changes. | v0.10 flesh-out, Q7, Q11; review M2, M7, S13 | Proposed |
| D422 | 2026-10-21 | **Seating is always a choice, never automatic.** An opening scene ends with "Seat it" (if a seat is free) or "Continue" and "Not now"; no Order seats itself, at an opening, a load or a migration. This keeps every simulator player other than the Orderer unchanged (D417). The new-warden step carries previous seats over by default, which for a player who never seated an Order is none. | v0.10 flesh-out | Proposed |
